decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client confirms using the add-bookmark flow and pasting a link.
decisions.note: The presented add flow saves a bookmark from a URL, conforming to the reference during the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, delete ... bookmarks.” The presentation does not identify which fields can be edited, and the client does not test or clarify post-save editing.
decisions.note: Editing is presented, but evidence cannot establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, delete ... bookmarks.” The client offers no contrary observation.
decisions.note: The recorded delete-bookmark behavior conforms during the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search across titles, notes, domains, and tags.” Round 1 client positively mentions “search” but does not address the missing description field or the distinction between domains and complete URLs.
decisions.note: The presented searchable fields omit descriptions and specify domains rather than full URLs. The client's general approval does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says search covers “tags,” but gives no query syntax. Round 1 client only refers generally to “search.”
decisions.note: Tag search is presented, but the record cannot establish whether the required #tag syntax is supported.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Grid and list layouts.” Round 1 client says the app is “clean” and mentions “grid/list views,” without identifying which fields each item exposes.
decisions.note: A list view exists, but the transcript cannot establish whether every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon as required.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Alphabetical and newest-first sorting.” Round 1 client acknowledges “sorting.”
decisions.note: Title/alphabetical and date-added/newest sorting are reference-conforming sort choices.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client, reacting to the maker's add flow: “it asks me to type in the title ... myself” and requests that pasting a URL “fills in the page's title and a short description ... automatically.”
decisions.note: At the initial implementation review, the manual metadata flow diverges from automatic collection. The client explicitly supplies the conforming title-and-description behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents automatic fetching of only “the page title and description.” Round 2 client repeats that title and description populated and says, “That's exactly what I was after,” without mentioning favicon or preview-image collection.
decisions.note: The revised metadata implementation remains incomplete relative to automatic title, description, favicon, and preview-image collection. The client does not express the remaining difference, so the approval is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents bookmark editing. Round 2 maker says generated details remain “fully editable”; Round 2 client confirms, “I could still edit them before saving.”
decisions.note: Taken together, the presented edit capability and editable generated fields conform to editing collected title and description before and after saving.
